target_customer: Companies and professionals needing furnished mid-term housing (corporate rentals of one month or more)
problem: Traditional corporate housing was dated and hotels and short-term rentals were poorly suited to multi-month stays.
business_model: Tech-enabled property manager leasing and furnishing homes and renting them to corporate clients

founders.name: Kulveer Taggar
founders.background_notes: YC page says Zeus reached over 450 million dollars in revenue before sale to Blueground in late 2023 and that he later started Phosphor Capital.

founders.name: Srini Panguluri
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a two-time YC founder with two exits.

founders.name: Joe Wong
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a two-time YC founder with two exits.

exit.reason: YC page states the company was sold to Blueground in late 2023; price not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly operations, leasing and furnishing; software for listing, pricing and property management was standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Operating scale and leases gave some advantage, but a capital heavy model with many rivals meant little structural protection.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Airbnb invested in the Series B in December 2019, and in 2023 competitor Blueground bought the company.

market_need_then: Companies relocating staff for months used legacy corporate housing such as Oakwood; Zeus pitched local flair and modern service, and press in 2019 described a growing furnished rentals segment.

branding.domain_note: Used zeusliving.com (the exact zeus.com was not recorded as owned); the domain did not resolve from this session's network.

identity.visual_style: Local design flair in furnished homes, per Skift
identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as living as a service

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press covered funding and expansion but no coverage of the brand itself; the Zeus name is shared by many unrelated companies.

outcome_analysis: Zeus Living raised a 24 million dollar round in March 2019 and a 55 million dollar Series B at a reported 205 million post-money in December 2019 with Airbnb among the investors, then was reported to have raised about 15 million at roughly half that valuation in 2020 and was sold to rival Blueground in late 2023. The step down in valuation and sale to a competitor point to a capital heavy model that could not hold its peak valuation, but sources did not state the cause so unit economics is a judgment.
notes: Batch conflict: YC lists Summer 2011 while Zeus Living is dated 2015 or 2016 by other sources and the YC bios mention a 2011 exit; the relationship between the S11 company and Zeus Living is not explained in sources I saw. Unverified: one source reports a 2.5M seed and an 11.5M Series A led by Initialized; a 2020 raise of about 15M equity and debt at about 110M was in one outlet only. Totals vary (79.1M to 161M). The 24M round stage is not stated in the headline so it is recorded as other. The Zeus 2019 competitor list (Sonder, Domio, 2nd Address) is from 2019 and not near founding so competitors are left empty. Founder education and prior employers not found.
